The build

Speech in.
Captions out.

Nepali, Maithili or English audio to a timed .srt / .vtt file.

Same language, or translated into either of the other two.

Gemma 4 is not a component. It is the system.

Audio in. Captions out.
Nothing in between.

No Whisper. No cloud speech API.
Take Gemma out and there is nothing left to demo.

9

behaviours from one adapter: 3 transcription, 6 translation directions. Selected by instruction, not by a router.

How it is trained

  • LoRA fine-tune · Gemma 4 E4B, audio-native, via Transformers + PEFT
  • Multitask mix · captioning and speech translation trained together, not bolted on after
  • Kept balanced · no task allowed to dominate. Nine good behaviours, not one plus eight demos.
  • E4B on purpose — edge-deployable. A clinic should not ship a patient's appointment to a cloud API.

Same held-out clips · both models · identical decoding

41.96% → 12.35%

Word error rate, lower is better

71%
less word error
72%
less char error

At 42% you get captions you cannot trust.
At 12% you get captions you can follow.

How the number was measured

One model, measured
against itself.

Same clips, both models, identical decoding. Held out of training, and not picked after we saw the results. No number off a training curve.

The accuracy figures are 100 minus the error rate. Readable indicators, not classification accuracy.

What happens after today

  • Then real-time streaming captions
  • Then on-device — a district clinic, no internet at all
